statement: MCA is component separation, not inherently semantic classification.
MCA is additive; component reconstructions need not have mutually exclusive pixel ownership.
Frequency alone is not morphology; scale, orientation, locality, elongation and coherence matter.
Do not call a component silhouette, intricacy, text or noise until garment data supports that interpretation.
Use the minimum dictionary set that yields stable interpretable separation.
Start with generic fixed dictionaries before learned garment-specific dictionaries.
Residual structure, not enthusiasm, should justify adding another dictionary.
MCA can support nuisance separation, structural factorization, or multi-branch representation.
Morphology may tell what a structure looks like; context/topology may be required to tell what it means.
Garment sketches may admit a useful factorization into global structural geometry and localized internal/detail structure.
A two-dictionary fixed MCA may be sufficient for an initial garment experiment.
No specific pair such as curvelet+wavelet or curvelet+DCT is yet designated as the garment solution.
